# COR040 `use-all`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

A `use` statement imports everything (no `only:` list).

## Why

Without `only:` every public entity of the module enters the scope: names collide or shadow local
ones silently, and a reader cannot tell where a name comes from. `only:` makes the dependency
explicit and keeps scopes small.

## Reported

```fortran
use penf
```

## Preferred

```fortran
use penf, only: R8P, I4P
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[COR040] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = COR040` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/cookbook/analysis#choose-the-rules).
